flashcards.back: "You are as You have said, yet I wish to see Your divine cosmic form."

flashcards.front: Why give Arjuna a divine eye? (11.8)
flashcards.back: He cannot see the cosmic form with physical eyes, so Krishna gives him the divine eye.
God everywhere, with infinite forms, arms, faces and eyes, and no beginning, middle or end.
The form holds all beings, worlds and time, and is both awe-inspiring and terrifying: beyond human grasp.
The warriors are already destroyed by God's will; Arjuna is only the instrument. We act, but are not the doers.

flashcards.front: Can study or ritual show this form? (11.53)
flashcards.back: No: not the Vedas, austerity, charity or ritual.

flashcards.front: How then can God be seen?
flashcards.back: By devotional love. He can be seen in any form the devotee holds dear; he returns to his gentle human form for Arjuna.

flashcards.front: The whole practice in one verse (11.55)
flashcards.back: Dedicate all work to God, make him the supreme goal, be devoted, unattached, and without enmity toward any being.

quiz.text: What does Arjuna ask to see in 11.3?
quiz.why: Every seeker's deepest longing: to see the Divine directly.

quiz.text: How can Arjuna see the cosmic form?

options.C: With a divine eye God gives him

quiz.text: How does Arjuna react to the vision?
quiz.why: The form is overwhelming, beyond comprehension.

options.A: Act, knowing God is the real doer

quiz.why: The outcome is already in God's will; we do our part.

quiz.text: Per 11.53, which reveals the four-armed form?

options.B: One who sees the cosmic form
options.C: One devoted, unattached, without enmity, working for God

quiz.why: The complete practice in one verse.
